violations.text: Molluscan shellfish tags were observed not dated with the last date of use. Shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

The chlorine sanitizer concentration for the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher was 0 parts per million (ppm). Chlorine sanitizing solutions must be between 50-100 ppm. The bottle of sanitizer was checked and changed. The sanitizer cycle was then rechecked at the time of inspection at the proper concentration of 50-100ppm. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

Beer Cheese and Pulled Pork were observed held at 122 and 129 degrees Fahrenheit respectively in the back area hot hold steam table. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items were properly reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit at time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

Several food items in the walk-in cooler and the cold rails were observed held at 47-62 degrees Fahrenheit. Food items recently stocked were moved to colder refrigeration. Food items in/taken from the walk-in cooler were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

The following items were observed improperly stored to prevent possible contamination: - Chemicals (glass cleaner) were stored on the same shelf with food/equipment/single service articles (on the prep table) in the kitchen area. - Medicine bottle was observed stored over the prep sink in the kitchen Chemical bottle and medicine were moved for proper storage at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

At the time of inspection, Reduced Oxygen Packaged Seafood (Lobster) was observed thawed in the walk-in cooler in its intact packaging. REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration. Due to temperature observed at 56 degrees Fahrenheit, lobster was voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026

At the time of inspection, the walk-in cooler was observed to be maintaining an ambient temperature of 62 degrees Fahrenheit with food temperatures observed at 56-58 degrees Fahrenheit. Service technician was called and arrived during inspection for service. Unit is not to be used for storage of Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Foods until properly maintaining ambient temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. New Violation. Correct By: 06/17/2026
The hand-washing sink in the bars was lacking paper towels. Paper towels provided at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024

Per the PIC, poultry (Chicken Wings) were partially cooked to 145 degrees Fahrenheit prior to cooling and storing in refrigeration. Poultry must be cooked to 165 degrees Fahrenheit or above for 15 seconds. Chicken wings were fully cooked at the time of inspection as corrective action. PIC is to submit request for approval to RIDOH CFP Supervisor to perform partial cooking of chicken wings. PIC is to discontinue partial cooking of items until granted approval from RIDOH CFP Supervisor. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024

Chowder and Meatballs, which were previously cooked and cooled, were placed in the hot hold steam unit and observed only reheated to 114 and 123 degrees Fahrenheit respectively for hot holding. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding must be rapidly reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit or above for 15 seconds. PIC placed food items on the cooktop and rapidly reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024

Several food items in the walk-in cooler were observed held at 44 - 45 degrees Fahrenheit (unit ambient temperature observed at 53 degrees Fahrenheit). Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Per the PIC, food items were recently delivered and moved to colder refrigeration at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024

The ice scoops at the bars were observed to be stored in with the juice bottles between uses. During pauses in food preparation, utensils must be stored on a clean surface or in a clean, protected location to prevent possible contamination. Ice scoops were moved to a separate container at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024

At the time of inspection, the Walk-In Cooler was observed to be in need of repair/adjustment. The unit was observed to be maintaining an ambient temperature of 53 degrees Fahrenheit with a large buildup of ice on the condenser unit. Food items were moved to colder refrigeration for proper storage at the time of inspection. PIC immediately began to defrost unit. Walk-In Cooler is not to be used for storage of TCS Foods until repaired/adjusted and properly maintaining an ambient temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. New Violation. Correct By: 08/29/2024
